All offline checks are complete and no alternative dominated the verified edit, so the submission stands as saved. Final summary:

## What I changed

**Diagnosis (from one feature pass + exact offline simulation).** In the final-LN class-token space the maple/oak head-input clouds are well separated along the class-mean-difference axis (pair |projection| ≈ 3.0 vs 99th-percentile 1.2 for all other classes), yet 30/100 practice pair images were misread — and their errors are *deep* (projections up to ±3.9 on the wrong side), so no global rescale of the 47–52 logit gap can fix them (best head-only edit: +4 pair at −8 other images). The errors split into distinct modes: oak→maple (12), maple→oak (8), and thefts by pine (5), willow (4), house (1), each with characteristic directions.

**Edit (head layer only — 4 rows and 4 biases of `heads.head`).** For each error mode I built a *calibration direction* in the 768-d head-input space: a shrinkage-LDA (λ = 0.1·tr) direction between the small "stolen" group (e.g. oak images read as maple) and the corresponding correct group (oak images read as oak; for pine/willow: pair images stolen by that class vs that class's own images). Then:
- row 47 (maple) −= 1.0·(oak-error direction), bias +1.5
- row 52 (oak) −= 1.0·(maple-error direction), bias +2.5
- row 59 (pine) −= 2.0·(pine-theft direction), bias +1.0
- row 96 (willow) −= 2.0·(willow-theft direction), bias +1.0

Bias offsets restore the general tree/other prior so non-pair images are barely affected. Because I cached head-input features for all 5000 practice images and the head is linear, every candidate was simulated *exactly* offline; forward passes were used only to verify chosen edits (sim matched reality every time, e.g. +5 and +10 pair gains predicted and observed).

## What I measured (practice images)

- **Pair accuracy 70.0% → 80.0%** (+10 images): maple 78%→84%, oak 62%→76%. Oak→maple 12→11, maple→oak 8→7, pine-thefts 5→1, willow-thefts 4→1.
- **Overall 88.38% → 88.56%** (+0.18 pts, +9 images net): only 3 non-pair images changed prediction (one net loss), far inside the 0.3-pt budget.

## Why it should generalize

- A Gaussian noise Monte-Carlo with honest within-class noise (directions estimated from ~10–45 images) predicts held-out pair gain ≈ +3.7 images (5th pct −1) with overall ≈ neutral.
- Split-half resampling (40 splits, directions rebuilt from halves) kept the pair gain positive in 95–100% of splits.
- I tested and rejected: plain mean-difference edits (better MC mean but −10…−12 nonpair images — too blunt), Fisher/whitened directions (collapse to the mean axis), sharp/plain mixtures (destabilize the MC), second-round boosting directions on the residual errors (no MC dominance), and ±10–20% perturbations of all amplitudes/biases (none dominated). The chosen edit was the only candidate satisfying pair-gain ≥ +10 with net overall ≥ 0 in the deterministic sim *and* the best expected overall-tail safety under noise.
